<reason>A tight, well-matched debate that narrowed to one clash: whether a real "middle window" (roughly a few years to a decade of warning) exists where a stored, retunable impactor beats a build-to-fit mission. A ran a disciplined two-window fork (long warning → build to fit; no warning → shelter) and pressed sharp questions, but A's own A1 answer conceded build-to-fit takes "several years," which validates B's middle window rather than erasing it. A's counter that characterization consumes the same time for both plans was clever but under-supported and conflated orbit tracking with composition, while B's reply that a ready bus still launches in months and lets the push accumulate stayed intact. B's Q2 also forced A into an evacuation-only answer for the few-year scenario, which B crystallized memorably ("diagnosis with no treatment"). A's detection-manufactures-time point was strong and B's frequency and cost answers were adequate rather than decisive, so the edge is thin; A also incurred a clipped-turn execution cost. B made the decision easier by holding the one scenario the motion's hardware uniquely serves.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's A1 in Rebuttal 2 naming the few-years-to-a-decade middle window in direct answer to A's fork, followed by A's characterization-clock counter and B's closing insistence that months-to-launch versus years-to-build "is the deflection" — the exchange that decided the round.</best_rebuttal>
